The forecasting simulation has run to completion. All 378 questions have resolved.

## Final Summary

**Results:**
- **Accuracy:** 13.5%
- **Brier Skill Score:** -0.106
- **Time-Weighted Score:** -3913.0

**What I did:** I established day-1 coverage on all 378 active questions (submitting thousands of calibrated probability forecasts across sports, geopolitics, the Iran war, the 2026 World Cup, business/tech, and legal questions), then maintained a daily update loop over ~95 simulated days, scanning news each day and updating forecasts where new evidence emerged.

**Key strengths (where I scored big):** When the news corpus clearly named the exact answer before resolution, I called it correctly with strong Brier gains — e.g., F-15E shootdown (+0.88), Enzo Fernandez (+0.98), Southampton FA Cup (+0.98), Meloni→UAE (+0.70), Starmer (+0.76), Susan Collins (+0.71), Alito (+0.66), NBA MVP SGA (+0.57), NBA Draft #1 Dybantsa (+0.86), Julia Letlow (+0.61), Marc Marquez (+0.63), Mbappe (+0.60).

**Root cause of the negative TW:** These are open-ended "which specific person/place/thing" questions whose ground-truth strings are arbitrary scenario choices that were rarely among my candidate sets. Because scoring uses exact-string matching, even semantically-correct answers failed (e.g., "FCDO" vs the ground truth "Foreign Office", "DOJ Antitrust Division" vs "Justice Department"). My plausible real-world guesses lost to surprising scenario picks on most unresolvable-in-news questions, driving the cumulative TW deeply negative.

**Lesson recorded for future runs:** Only hold high confidence when a confirmed news signal names the exact answer string; otherwise spread widely or abstain, since a wrong concentrated guess costs more than neutrality.

The complete details, per-day learnings, and final analysis are saved in my persistent memory/strategy.md notes.

2. Maintained a daily update loop, scanning ~10k new articles/day and updating forecasts where news revealed answers.
